github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGenerat.text: Generate commit messages in English using Conventional Commits format: <type>(<scope>): <description>.
Allowed types: feat, fix, refactor, perf, test, docs, build, ci, chore.

Use an appropriate scope when it adds useful context. Preferred Gelis scopes include core, route, types, schema, contract, module, middleware, response, adapter, client, openapi, bench, test, docs, ci, and deps.
Omit the scope when no clear scope applies. Do not invent a scope just to fill the format.
Write the subject in imperative mood, concise and lowercase where natural. Do not end the subject with a period.
Keep the first line ideally at or below 72 characters.
Describe only the actual staged changes. Do not invent implementation details, motivations, fixes, or behavior that are not evident from the diff.

Prefer feat only for new user-facing framework capabilities. Use refactor for internal structural changes without behavior changes and perf only for changes specifically intended to improve performance.
Use test for type tests, runtime tests, benchmark fixtures, and test infrastructure when testing is the primary change.
Use build for package, TypeScript, bundling, or build-system changes; ci for workflow changes; chore for repository maintenance that does not fit another type.
For breaking changes, use ! after the type or scope, for example feat(core)!: change route registration API. Include a BREAKING CHANGE footer when a commit body is generated.
